info.title: PHOENIX Panel API
info.description: Programmatic interface to a PHOENIX panel. Authenticate either by logging in (cookie) or with an API token from Settings → Security → API Token (Bearer). All endpoints under /panel/api/* honour both modes — an API token is a full-admin credential, so treat it like the panel password.

AmneziaWGLogs.description:
AmneziaWGLogs is what the overview's AmneziaWG log view renders: the live
per-peer activity of every running embedded interface, plus the panel's
own recent AmneziaWG lifecycle log lines that explain a peer being absent
from Peers at all.

example: 2025/01/01 12:00:00 amneziawg: started interface awg1 for inbound 1

lastUsedAt.description: unix millis of the last successful authentication

prefix.description: leading plaintext characters, for identifying a token in the list

token.description: SHA-256 hash; the plaintext is shown only once at creation

Client.description: Client represents a client configuration for Xray inbounds with traffic limits and settings.

activateBefore.description:
ActivateBefore is the delayed-start activation deadline (ms). While the
client is still un-activated (negative expiryTime) past this timestamp,
the client is treated as expired. 0 disables the deadline.

limitDevice.description:
LimitDevice caps how many distinct HWID-identified devices may fetch
this client's subscription. 0 (the default) disables both tracking and
enforcement, so existing clients are unaffected.

privateKey.description:
Native WireGuard/AmneziaWG peer material. These fields remain optional
for the other Xray protocols and are persisted with the shared client
record so one client identity can be attached to several inbounds.

renewalMode.description:
RenewalMode selects the auto-renew schedule used when a renewal fires:
0 = rolling whole Reset-day steps (legacy behavior), 1 = whole calendar
months, 2 = a fixed weekday (RenewalDay).

ClientTraffic.description:
ClientTraffic represents traffic statistics and limits for a specific client.
It tracks upload/download usage, expiry times, and online status for inbound clients.

FallbackParentInfo.description:
FallbackParentInfo carries everything the frontend needs to rewrite a
child inbound's client link: where to connect (the master's address
and port) and which path matched on the master's fallbacks array.
The frontend already has the master inbound in its dbInbounds list,
so we only ship identifiers + the match path here.

HistoryOfSeeders.description: HistoryOfSeeders tracks which database seeders have been executed to prevent re-running.

Inbound.description: Inbound represents an Xray inbound configuration with traffic statistics and settings.

fallbackParent.description:
FallbackParent is populated by the API layer when this inbound is
attached as a fallback child of a VLESS/Trojan TCP-TLS master.
The frontend uses it to rewrite client-share links so they advertise
the master's externally reachable endpoint instead of the child's
loopback listen. Not persisted.

originNodeGuid.description:
OriginNodeGuid is the panelGuid of the node that physically hosts this
inbound, propagated up across hops (#4983). Empty for an inbound that
lives on this panel's own xray; set to the originating node's GUID when
the inbound was synced from a node (kept as-is across further hops). Lets
the master attribute a deeply nested inbound to the real node instead of
the intermediate one it was fetched through.

subSortIndex.description: 1-based sort order of this inbound's links in subscription output only (lower first; ties by id)

InboundClientIps.description: InboundClientIps stores IP addresses associated with inbound clients for access control.

nodeId.description:
Hosting node; nil for this panel's own inbounds. Lets the clients
page map a node filter onto inbound IDs (#4997).

L2TPInboundOption.description:
L2TPInboundOption is the non-client portion of the native connection
parameters needed by the admin Client Information dialog. Client username
and password stay in the selected client record and are never broadcast as
part of the inbound picker response.

Msg.description: Msg represents a standard API response message with success status, message text, and optional data object.

success.description: Indicates if the operation was successful

Node.description:
Node represents a remote PHOENIX panel registered with the central panel.
The central panel polls each node's existing /panel/api/server/status
endpoint over HTTP using the per-node ApiToken to populate the runtime
status fields below.

guid.description:
Guid is the remote panel's stable self-identifier (its panelGuid),
learned from each heartbeat. It is the globally stable node identity used
to attribute online clients/inbounds to the physical node across a chain
of nodes (#4983); panel-local autoincrement ids don't survive a hop.
Observed-state only — never user-edited.

parentGuid.description:
ParentGuid + Transitive are set only when a node is surfaced as part of a
node tree (#4983): direct nodes carry the master panel's own GUID, a
transitive sub-node carries its parent node's GUID. Transitive nodes are
read-only projections (Id == 0, not persisted) — never edited or deployed.

status.description:
Heartbeat-updated fields. UpdatedAt advances on every probe even when
the row is otherwise unchanged so the UI's "last seen" tooltip is
truthful without us having to read LastHeartbeat separately.
online|offline|unknown

xrayState.description:
XrayState and XrayError are captured from the remote node's /panel/api/server/status
during heartbeats. They let the central panel distinguish "panel API reachable"
(status=online) from "Xray core itself has failed on the node" for monitoring.

OutboundTraffics.description: OutboundTraffics tracks traffic statistics for Xray outbound connections.

PeerActivity.description:
PeerActivity is one peer's live embedded-Device-reported state, the
counterpart of an Xray access-log entry: a tunnel logs no requests, only
handshakes and bytes.

handshake.description: Handshake is unix milliseconds, 0 when the peer has never connected.

xrayState.description:
XrayState/XrayError are populated on successful probes even when the node's
Xray core is not healthy. The UI uses them for a distinct "panel ok, xray failed" indicator.

ServerSettings.description:
ServerSettings is the "server" block of an AmneziaWG inbound's Settings
JSON: the interface-level configuration shared by every client/peer. The
listen port is deliberately not duplicated here — it lives on the inbound
row itself (Inbound.Port), like every other protocol.

externalInterface.description:
ExternalInterface, IPv6Enabled, and IPv6ExternalInterface are live
again as of Phase 3.5 -- see the matching fields on Instance for what
they gate (internal/amneziawgnet's IPv6-address-alias mechanism).
IPv6Subnet was never actually vestigial either: InstanceFromInbound
already consumes it (via serverAddressV6) to build the server's own
tunnel address, same as always. Only RouteThroughXray, below, remains
genuinely vestigial as of the hard cutover to the embedded path
(internal/amneziawgnet) -- read from existing stored settings for
backward compatibility, but not acted on by anything.

headerProtectionKey.description:
HeaderProtectionKey and ContentPaddingAddition are AmneziaWG 3.0
fields, flat and top-level for the same tools/openapigen reason as
the block above; Obfuscation() below folds them back into
Obfuscation31's own identically named fields.
HeaderProtectionKey is a base64 32-byte key; empty (the default)
disables AWG 3.0 header protection. A non-empty value requires
every one of S1-S4 above to be >= 12 -- ValidateObfuscation
enforces this at save time, not just at IpcSet time.
ContentPaddingAddition is a "low-high" range or bare integer, the
same grammar and uint32 cap as H1-H4.

jc.description:
Obfuscation31's fields, repeated flat (not embedded) rather than
nested under their own key: encoding/json would happily inline an
embedded Obfuscation31 the same way, but the frontend's Go->Zod/TS
generator (tools/openapigen) does not — it emits a genuinely nested
`obfuscation31` object, which would silently diverge from the real
wire JSON. See Obfuscation() below for the manager-facing conversion.

primaryDns.description:
PrimaryDNS/SecondaryDNS seed client configs' DNS line. Blank is
meaningful, so no omitempty: a dropped key resurrects frontend defaults.

randomTrailers.description:
RandomTrailers/DisableCookies mirror Instance's identically named
AmneziaWG 3.1 fields -- see that type's own doc comment for the real
protocol/interop details. Both real bool fields (not omitempty):
buildUAPIConfig always emits both lines explicitly so the
reconfigure-in-place diff correctly notices a true->false edit, not
just false->true.

rekeyAfterTime.description:
RekeyAfterTime/RekeyTimeout/RejectAfterTime/KeepaliveTimeout/
MaxHandshakeAttempts mirror Instance's identically named fields --
see that type's own doc comment for the grammar/width/real-default
details. Flat and top-level for the same tools/openapigen reason as
the rest of this struct.

Setting.description: Setting stores key-value configuration settings for the PHOENIX panel.

User.description: User represents a user account in the PHOENIX panel.

tags.name: Authentication
tags.description: Two authentication modes are supported. UI sessions use a cookie set by the login endpoint. Programmatic clients (bots, scripts, remote panels) authenticate with a Bearer token taken from Settings → Security → API Token. Both work for every endpoint under /panel/api/*.

tags.name: Inbounds
tags.description: Manage inbound configurations and their clients. All endpoints live under /panel/api/inbounds and require a logged-in session or Bearer token. Link-generating endpoints honour forwarded headers only when the request comes from a configured trusted proxy.

tags.name: Server
tags.description: System status, log retrieval, certificate generators, Xray binary management, and backup/restore. All under /panel/api/server.

tags.name: Clients
tags.description: Manage clients as first-class entities that can be attached to one or more inbounds. A single client row drives the settings.clients entry in every inbound it belongs to. Endpoints live under /panel/api/clients.

tags.name: Nodes
tags.description: Manage remote PHOENIX panels acting as nodes for a central panel. All endpoints under /panel/api/nodes.

tags.name: Backup
tags.description: Operations that interact with the configured Telegram bot.

tags.name: Settings
tags.description: Panel configuration and user credentials. All endpoints live under /panel/api/setting and require a logged-in session or Bearer token.

tags.name: API Tokens
tags.description: Manage Bearer tokens used for programmatic auth (bots, central panels acting on this node, CI). Each token has a unique name and an enabled flag — disable to revoke without deleting, delete to revoke permanently. Tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes and the plaintext is returned only once, in the create response — it cannot be retrieved afterwards, so copy it then. Send one as Authorization: Bearer <token> on any /panel/api/* request — the token is a full-admin credential.

tags.name: Xray Settings
tags.description: Xray configuration template, outbound management, Warp/Nord integration, and config testing. All endpoints under /panel/api/xray.

tags.name: Subscription Server
tags.description: A separate HTTP/HTTPS server that serves proxy subscription links (standard, JSON, and Clash) to clients. The server listens on its own port (default 10882) and is configured in Settings → Subscription. Paths are configurable; defaults are shown below. All subscription endpoints set response headers for client apps to read traffic/expiry info.

tags.name: Resellers (نمایندگی)
tags.description: Panel sub-accounts that own a slice of the panel: their own inbounds, their own clients, and two quotas (clients, traffic). Inbounds are attached by the admin via the Attach Inbound list — the reseller can only see/manage assigned inbounds. A reseller signs in with its own username/password on the same login page; its session reads /panel/api/inbounds/* and /panel/api/reseller/*, manages its clients under /panel/api/clients/* and reaches /panel/api/auth/me — inbound writes and everything else answer 403. The endpoints below are the admin-side management API under /panel/api/resellers; a wrong-owner access answers 403 with inbound not found / client not found.

tags.name: Reseller Wallet Top-up (Public)
tags.description: Anonymous wallet deposit checkout using a signed reseller link. A pending reseller_deposit order is credited only after the existing HMAC-verified payment webhook confirms its amount.

tags.name: Reseller Signup (Public)
tags.description: Anonymous customer registration from a signed, expiring reseller invitation. Each link is bound to one reseller and one plan template; current reseller activity, inbound ownership, and quotas are revalidated at submission.

tags.name: Client Checkout (Public)
tags.description: Anonymous, link-based client checkout. A signed per-client ref token (issued via /panel/api/clients/checkout-link/:email) authorizes every call; no panel session is required. Orders are recorded as pending and completed by the payment webhook.

tags.name: WebSocket
tags.description: Real-time status updates via WebSocket. Connect once at ws:///ws to receive a stream of JSON messages without polling. Requires an authenticated session cookie (Bearer token auth is not supported). Each message has a type field that identifies the payload shape.

post.summary: Authenticate with username + password and receive a session cookie. Required before any cookie-based API call.

twoFactorCode.description: OTP code when 2FA is enabled. Omit otherwise.

post.summary: Clear the session cookie. Requires the CSRF header for browser sessions.

get.summary: Mint a CSRF token for the current session. The SPA replays it in the X-CSRF-Token header on unsafe requests. Bearer-token callers can skip this — the middleware short-circuits CSRF for authenticated API requests.

post.summary: Returns whether 2FA is enabled on the panel — used by the login page to decide whether to show the OTP field.

get.summary: List every inbound owned by the authenticated user, including each inbound’s clientStats traffic counters. settings, streamSettings, and sniffing are returned as nested JSON objects (no escaped strings); legacy callers that send them back as JSON-encoded strings are still accepted on write.

Same shape as /list but with settings.clients[] stripped down to {email, enable, comment} and ClientStats not enriched with UUID/SubId. Use this for list pages; fetch /get/:id when you need the full per-client payload (uuid, password, flow, ...).

Lightweight picker projection of the authenticated user’s inbounds. Returns id, remark, tag, protocol, port, a server-computed tlsFlowCapable flag (true for VLESS on TCP with tls or reality, or on XHTTP with VLESS encryption / vlessenc enabled), and ssMethod (the Shadowsocks cipher, empty for non-Shadowsocks inbounds — used by the client UI to generate a valid Shadowsocks 2022 PSK). Use this for dropdowns and attach pickers — it skips settings, streamSettings, and clientStats so the payload stays small even on panels with thousands of clients.
Fetch a single inbound by numeric ID.

post.summary: Create a new inbound. Send the full inbound payload (protocol, port, settings, streamSettings, sniffing, remark, expiryTime, total, enable). settings, streamSettings, and sniffing may be sent as nested JSON objects (preferred) or as JSON-encoded strings (legacy).
Delete an inbound by ID. Also removes its associated client stats rows.
Delete many inbounds in one call. Processes the list sequentially; failures are reported per id and the rest still proceed. Restarts xray at most once.
Replace an inbound’s configuration. Body shape mirrors /add. Heavy on inbounds with thousands of clients — prefer /setEnable for enable-only flips.
Toggle only the enable flag without serialising the whole settings JSON. Recommended for UI switches on large inbounds.
Zero out upload + download counters for a single inbound. Does not touch per-client counters.

Remove every client attached to a single inbound while keeping the inbound itself. Collects emails from settings.clients[] and feeds them into the optimized bulk-delete path (runtime user removal + traffic-row cleanup + SyncInbound). Destructive and cannot be undone.
Reset upload + download counters on every inbound. Destructive — accounting history is lost.
Bulk-import an inbound from a JSON blob (e.g. one exported via the UI). The body uses form encoding with a single "data" field.

Receive a master panel's aggregated per-client usage, keyed by the master's GUID. Stored in a side table used only for the UI display overlay and local quota enforcement — never folded into the local counters that masters poll, so delta accounting stays intact. Called panel-to-panel by the node traffic sync job.

masterGuid.description: Stable GUID of the pushing master panel.

traffics.description: Client traffic rows; only email/up/down are read.

get.summary: List the fallback rules attached to a master VLESS/Trojan TCP-TLS inbound. Each rule links one child inbound (the dest) to optional SNI/ALPN/path/dest/xver match criteria. When dest is empty the child inbound's listen+port is used.

post.summary: Replace the entire fallback list for a master inbound. Body is JSON. Triggers an Xray restart.

fallbacks.description: Array of {childId, name, alpn, path, dest, xver, sortOrder} entries. Leave dest empty to auto-resolve from the child inbound's listen+port; set it (e.g. "8443", "127.0.0.1:8443", "/dev/shm/x.sock") to override.

get.summary: Real-time machine snapshot: CPU, memory, swap, disk, network IO, load averages, open connections, Xray state. Cached and refreshed every 2 seconds in the background.
Legacy: aggregated CPU history. Use /history/cpu/:bucket instead — same data with a uniform {t, v} shape.
Aggregated time-series for one metric. Returns an array of {t, v} samples covering the last ~6 hours.

parameters.name: metric
parameters.description: cpu | mem | netUp | netDown | online | load1 | load5 | load15.

get.summary: Xray runtime metrics state — whether the xray config has a `metrics` block, which expvar keys are flowing, and the current snapshot values for each. Returns an empty state when metrics are not configured.
Time-series history for one Xray runtime metric over the last ~6 hours. Same {t, v} shape as /history/:metric/:bucket.
Latest snapshot from the Xray observatory — per-outbound latency, health status, and last-probe time. Only populated when the Xray config has an observatory configured.
Time-series of observatory probe results for one outbound tag. Same {t, v} shape as the other history endpoints.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Outbound tag from the observatory config.

get.summary: Check GitHub for the highest compatible Xray-core release available for this host.
Check whether a newer PHOENIX release is available on GitHub. Pass ?force=true to bypass the short-lived server-side cache.
Return the assembled Xray config that’s currently running on this host.
Stream the SQLite database file as an attachment. Use as a manual backup.
Stream a cross-engine migration file as an attachment: a .dump (SQL text) on SQLite, or a .db SQLite database built from the live data on PostgreSQL.
Generate a fresh UUID v4. Convenience helper for client IDs.

Return this panel's own web TLS certificate and key file paths. The central panel calls it on a node (via the node API token) so "Set Cert from Panel" fills a node-assigned inbound with paths that exist on the node.

Read-only summaries (guid, parentGuid, name, address, status, versions) of the nodes this panel manages. A parent panel calls it on a node (via the node API token) to surface transitive sub-nodes in a chained topology. Counts are computed by the parent, not returned here.
Generate a new X25519 keypair for Reality.
Generate a new ML-DSA-65 keypair (post-quantum signature). Returns {privateKey, publicKey, seed}.
Generate a new ML-KEM-768 keypair (post-quantum KEM). Returns {clientKey, serverKey}.
Generate VLESS encryption auth options. Returns an auths array each with id, label, encryption, and decryption fields.

post.summary: Stop the Xray binary. All proxies go offline immediately.
Reload Xray with the current config. Typically required after structural inbound or routing changes.
Stop all managed OpenVPN daemons and hold reconciliation until the service is started again. Returns after the manager has stopped the processes.
Resume the managed OpenVPN service and reconcile enabled OpenVPN inbounds immediately.
Stop and start the managed OpenVPN daemons using the current inbound configuration.
Resume OpenVPN reconciliation and apply the current OpenVPN inbound configuration.
Stop the managed L2TP/IPsec daemon group and hold reconciliation until the service is started again.
Resume the managed L2TP/IPsec service and reconcile the enabled L2TP inbound immediately.
Stop and start the managed L2TP/IPsec daemon group using the current inbound configuration.
Resume L2TP/IPsec reconciliation and apply the current inbound configuration.
Download, verify, and install the latest compatible Xray-core release; failed updates roll back automatically.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: Version tag returned by getXrayVersion; the server accepts only the current compatible release.

post.summary: Self-update the panel to the latest version. The server restarts on success.
Refresh the default GeoIP / GeoSite data files. Body can include a fileName, or use the /:fileName variant.

fileName.description: Filename to update (e.g. geoip.dat, geosite.dat). Omit to update all defaults.

post.summary: Refresh a single Geo file by filename (e.g. geoip.dat, geosite.dat).

parameters.name: fileName
parameters.description: Filename of the data file to refresh.

post.summary: Return the last N lines of the panel’s own log.
Return the last N lines of the Xray process log.

filter.description: Keyword filter — only lines containing this string.

example.obj:
2025/01/01 12:00:00 rejected  vless  proxy  example.com  reason: no valid user
2025/01/01 12:00:01 direct  freedom  ok

post.summary: Return live AmneziaWG peer activity (handshake, endpoint, transfer) plus the panel’s own AmneziaWG event lines.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Maximum peer rows and event lines to return.

filter.description: Keyword filter — only rows/lines containing this string.

events: 2025/01/01 12:00:00 amneziawg: started interface awg1 for inbound 1

post.summary: Restore the panel DB from an uploaded SQLite file (multipart form, field name "db"). The panel restarts after restore. Destructive.
Generate a new ECH (Encrypted Client Hello) keypair and config list for the given SNI.

sni.description: Server Name Indication to generate the ECH config for.

get.summary: Fetch the fully aggregated inbound_client_ips database table. Used by nodes to sync recently active IPs across the cluster.

post.summary: Submit a list of recently active IP timestamps. The panel merges them with the existing database to maintain a unified global IP-limit view.

get.summary: List every client with its attached inbound IDs and traffic record. The reverse field, if set, is returned as a nested JSON object (legacy JSON-encoded-string form is still accepted on write).

Export a versioned client transfer envelope containing client credentials, multi-protocol fields, inbound attachments, and flow overrides. Resellers receive only their assigned clients and inbounds; traffic counters and database IDs are excluded.
Issue a signed, expiring public checkout link token for one client (resellers only for their own clients). Build the client URL as <basePath>/panel/checkout?ref=<token>.

Filter, sort, and paginate clients on the server. Each item is a slim row (no uuid/password/auth/flow/security/reverse/tgId) so the clients page can ship 25-ish rows in a few KB instead of the full table. The response also includes a summary computed across the full DB row set so dashboard counters stay stable as the user paginates or filters. Page size capped at 200; fetch /get/:email to obtain the full per-client payload for an edit/info modal.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 25, capped at 200.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match on email / subId / comment.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Status bucket: online | active | deactive | depleted | expiring.

parameters.name: protocol
parameters.description: Match clients attached to at least one inbound of this protocol (vless, vmess, trojan, shadowsocks, ...).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort key: enable | email | inboundIds | traffic | remaining | expiryTime.

get.summary: Fetch one client by email, including the inbound IDs it is attached to.

post.summary: Create a new client and attach it to one or more inbounds in a single call. Body is JSON. Per-protocol secrets (UUID for VLESS/VMess, password for Trojan/Shadowsocks, auth for Hysteria) are generated server-side when omitted, so callers can send only the universal fields.

client.description: Client fields: email, subId, id (uuid), password, auth, flow, totalGB, expiryTime, limitIp, tgId (numeric Telegram user ID, 0 = none), comment, enable.

inboundIds.description: Inbound IDs to attach the client to. At least one required.

post.summary: Preflight and import a versioned client transfer envelope. The operation rejects duplicate or colliding credentials, invalid attachments, and out-of-scope reseller data before mutating clients; the response reports created, updated, failed, and restart counts.

Update an existing client by email. Changes propagate to every attached inbound. Body is the JSON client payload — supply the full set of fields you want to keep (the server replaces the row, it does not patch).
Delete a client by email. Removes it from every attached inbound and drops its traffic record unless keepTraffic=1 is passed.

parameters.name: keepTraffic
parameters.description: Pass 1 to retain the xray_client_traffic row after deletion.

post.summary: Attach an existing client to one or more additional inbounds. Body is JSON.
Detach a client from one or more inbounds without deleting the client.
Reset the up/down counters for every client globally. Quotas and expiry are not affected. Triggers an Xray restart if any counter actually moved.

Delete every client whose traffic quota is exhausted (used >= total, when reset is disabled) or whose expiry has passed. Returns the deleted count and triggers an Xray restart when any client was on a running inbound.

Shift expiry and/or traffic quota for many clients in one call. addDays/addBytes may be negative. Clients with unlimited expiry (expiryTime=0) or unlimited traffic (totalGB=0) are skipped for the corresponding field — bulk extend never converts unlimited to limited. Returns the adjusted count and per-email skip reasons.

Delete many clients in one call. The server processes the list sequentially so each delete sees the committed state of the previous one — avoids the race the per-email fan-out had on the panel side. Pass keepTraffic=true to retain the xray_client_traffic rows after deletion.

Create many clients in one call. Body is a JSON array of {client, inboundIds} payloads — the same shape /add accepts. Items are processed sequentially; per-email skip reasons are returned for items that fail (e.g., duplicate email). Triggers a single Xray restart at the end if any inbound was running.

Add many clients to a group in one call. Updates clients.group_name and patches the matching client entry inside every owning inbound's settings JSON in a single transaction. If the group name does not yet exist (in client_groups or as a derived label), it is auto-created as a persistent group. To clear the group label, use /groups/bulkRemove instead.

Clear the group label on many clients in one call. Inverse of /groups/bulkAdd. Clients themselves are kept — only the group label is cleared from clients.group_name and from each owning inbound's settings JSON. Groups become empty if all their members are removed.

Attach many existing clients to many inbounds in one call. Each client keeps its identity (email/UUID/password/subId) and a shared traffic row; all clients are added to a target inbound in a single AddInboundClient call. Clients already present on a target are reported under skipped. Returns per-email attached/skipped/errors lists and triggers a single Xray restart if any target inbound was running.

emails.description: Emails of existing clients to attach.

inboundIds.description: Target inbound IDs to attach every client to.

post.summary: Mirror of bulkAttach: detach many existing clients from many inbounds in one call. For each email, intersects the client's current inbounds with the requested set and detaches from those only; (email, inbound) pairs where the client is not currently attached are silently no-ops. Emails not attached to any of the requested inbounds are reported under skipped. Client records are kept even if they become orphaned — use bulkDel for full removal. Returns per-email detached/skipped/errors lists and triggers a single Xray restart if any target inbound was running.

emails.description: Emails of existing clients to detach.

inboundIds.description: Inbound IDs to detach the clients from.

post.summary: Zero up/down counters for many clients in one call. Loops the single-reset path so each client is re-enabled across its attached inbounds and pushed to Xray/remote nodes. Returns the count of successfully reset clients.

get.summary: List all client groups with their member counts. Merges persisted groups (rows in client_groups, including empty placeholders) with the distinct group_name values currently set on clients. Sorted alphabetically (case-insensitive).
Return just the email list of clients that currently belong to the given group. Useful for fanning a single bulk action over an entire group without round-tripping the full client list.

post.summary: Create a new empty (placeholder) group. The group becomes selectable in client forms and the filter drawer even before any client is added to it. Errors if a group with the same name already exists.

Rename a group. The new name is applied to the client_groups row AND propagated to every matching client (both clients.group_name and the client entry inside every owning inbound's settings JSON) in a single transaction. Returns the number of clients whose label was updated.

Remove a group. Deletes the client_groups row and clears the group label from every matching client (both clients.group_name and the inbound settings JSON). The clients themselves are NOT deleted — use /bulkDel after filtering by group for that. Returns the count of clients whose label was cleared.
Zero out a single client’s up/down counters. Re-enables the client across every attached inbound and pushes the change to Xray (or the remote node) so depleted users can connect again immediately.
Manually adjust a client’s upload + download counters. Useful for migrations from external accounting systems.
List source IPs that have connected with the given client’s credentials. Returns an array of "ip (timestamp)" strings.
Reset the recorded IP list for a client.

get.summary: List HWID-registered devices for a client (device limit feature). Each entry carries hwid, ip, userAgent, createdAt and lastSeenAt. Only clients with a device limit register devices.

post.summary: Unregister one device (HWID) of a client, freeing a device slot so the user can register another device.
List the emails of currently connected clients (last seen within the heartbeat window), deduped across every node.

Online client emails grouped by the panelGuid of the node that physically hosts each client. The local panel uses its own GUID; each node (at any depth in a chain) uses its GUID. Lets the inbounds page attribute online status to the real node instead of the intermediate one it syncs through.

Inbound tags that carried traffic within the heartbeat window, grouped by the hosting node's panelGuid. Pairs with onlinesByGuid so the inbounds page only marks a multi-inbound client online on the inbounds it actually used. Nodes that do not report per-inbound activity are absent.
Map of client email → last-seen unix timestamp.

get.summary: Traffic counters for a client identified by email.

Return every protocol URL (vless://, vmess://, trojan://, ss://, hysteria://, hy2://) for clients matching the subscription ID. Same result set as /sub/<subId>, but as a JSON array — no base64. When an inbound has streamSettings.externalProxy set, one URL is emitted per external proxy. Empty array when the subId has no enabled clients.

parameters.name: subId
parameters.description: Subscription ID, taken from the client's subId field.

get.summary: Return every URL for one client across all attached inbounds — the same strings the Copy URL button copies in the panel UI. Supported protocols: vmess, vless, trojan, shadowsocks, hysteria. If streamSettings.externalProxy is set, returns one URL per external proxy. Protocols without a URL form (socks, http, mixed, wireguard, dokodemo, tunnel) contribute nothing.

Return the ready-to-import .ovpn profile for a client's openvpn inbound: client/dev/proto/remote plus the embedded CA, server certificate and the client's own keypair (CN = client email). Resellers may only fetch profiles of their own clients. Fails when the client has no enabled local openvpn inbound or the daemon has not provisioned the certificates yet.

obj.profile:
client
dev tun
proto udp
remote vpn.example.com 1194
...
<ca>
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
...
</ca>
<cert>
...
</cert>
<key>
...
</key>

get.summary: List every configured node with its connection details, health, and last heartbeat patch.
Fetch a single node by ID.

Fetch a node's own web TLS certificate/key file paths (proxied to the node). Used by the inbound form's "Set Cert from Panel" so a node-assigned inbound gets paths that exist on the node, not the central panel.

post.summary: Register a new remote node. Provide its URL, apiToken, and optional remark / allowPrivateAddress flag.
Replace a node’s connection details. Same body shape as /add.
Delete a node. Inbounds bound to it are not auto-migrated.
Pause or resume traffic sync with this node.
Probe a node without saving it. Uses the body as connection details and returns the same heartbeat snapshot a registered node would have.

Connect to the node over HTTPS without verifying its certificate and return the leaf certificate's SHA-256 (base64). Used by the Add/Edit Node dialog to fetch and pin a self-signed certificate. Uses the same body as /test.
Use unsaved node connection details to list the remote inbounds available for selective import.
Probe an existing node, updating its cached health state.

Trigger the official panel self-updater on each given node (downloads the latest release and restarts). Only enabled, online nodes are updated; offline/disabled ones are reported as skipped. Returns a per-node result list.

get.summary: Aggregated metric history for a node — same shape as /server/history, scoped to one node.

post.summary: Send a fresh DB backup to every Telegram chat configured as an admin recipient. No body, no params.
Return every panel setting: web server, Telegram bot, subscription, security, LDAP. The full JSON blob that the Settings page edits.
Return the computed default settings based on the request host. Useful to preview what a fresh install would use.
Persist every setting at once. The body mirrors the shape returned by /all. Invalid values (bad ports, missing cert pairs, etc.) are rejected before write.
Change the panel admin username and password. Requires the current credentials for verification. The session is refreshed with the new values on success.
Restart the entire PHOENIX process after a 3-second grace period. The connection drops immediately; the panel comes back online ~5-10 seconds later.

get.summary: Return the built-in default Xray JSON config template that ships with this panel version.
List every API token, enabled or not. The token value is never returned — only metadata.

post.summary: Mint a new API token. Name must be unique and 1-64 characters; the token string is server-generated and returned only in this response — it is stored hashed and cannot be retrieved later.

example.msg: a token with that name already exists

post.summary: Permanently delete a token. Any caller using it stops authenticating immediately.
Toggle a token enabled/disabled without deleting it. Disabled tokens are rejected by checkAPIAuth on the next request.

get.summary: Inspect the TLS certificate currently configured on the panel (subject, issuer, expiry, days left, self-signed flag).

post.summary: Issue a Let's Encrypt (RFC 8555 HTTP-01 on port 80, auto-renewed daily) or 1-year self-signed certificate and optionally apply its paths to the panel.

domain.description: Hostname (or IP for self-signed) to issue for.

applyToPanel.description: Save the new paths to webCertFile / webKeyFile (default true).

post.summary: Send a verification embed to the configured Discord Webhook URL and/or Bot channel.
Immediately upload a database snapshot to the configured S3 / Cloudflare R2 / MinIO or WebDAV cloud storage and apply retention cleanup.

get.summary: List recent security audit log entries with optional actorType, module, and search filters.

post.summary: Clear all recorded security audit log entries.
Return the Xray config template (JSON string), available inbound tags, client reverse tags, and the configured outbound test URL in one response.

get.summary: Return the built-in default Xray config shipped with the panel (identical to /panel/api/setting/getDefaultJsonConfig).
Return traffic statistics for every outbound. Each outbound shows up/down/total counters.
Return the most recent Xray process stdout/stderr output. Useful to check for startup errors or runtime warnings.

post.summary: Save the Xray JSON config template and optionally the outbound test URL. Both are sent as form fields.

outboundTestUrl.description: URL used for outbound reachability tests. Defaults to https://www.google.com/generate_204.

post.summary: Manage Cloudflare Warp integration. The action parameter selects the operation.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: data — return Warp stats (quota, remaining). del — delete Warp data. config — return current Warp config. reg — register a new Warp endpoint (sends privateKey, publicKey). regMasque — register a separate device enrolled for MASQUE and return its warp key pair, addresses and endpoint. license — set a Warp+ license key (sends license).

post.summary: Manage NordVPN integration. The action parameter selects the operation.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: countries — list available countries. servers — list servers in a country (sends countryId). reg — get NordVPN credentials (sends token). setKey — store NordVPN API key (sends key). data — return current NordVPN connection data. del — delete NordVPN data.

post.summary: Reset traffic counters for a specific outbound by tag.
Test an outbound configuration. Sends the outbound JSON (required), optionally all outbounds (to resolve sockopt.dialerProxy dependencies), and a mode flag.

allOutbounds.description: JSON array of all outbounds — used to resolve dialerProxy chains.

mode.description: "tcp" for a fast dial-only probe (parallel-safe). Default/empty uses a full HTTP probe through a temp xray instance.

post.summary: Test a batch of outbounds (max 50) through one shared temp xray instance. Returns an array of results in input order, each with the outbound tag, delay, HTTP status and a connect/TLS/TTFB timing breakdown.

outbounds.description: JSON array of outbound configs to test (required).

allOutbounds.description: JSON array of all outbounds — used to resolve dialerProxy chains.

mode.description: "tcp" for fast dial-only probes (UDP-transport outbounds are still probed over HTTP). Default/empty routes a real HTTP request through each outbound.

post.summary: Live state of routing balancers in the running core (RoutingService.GetBalancerInfo): current override and the targets the strategy prefers. Returns a map keyed by balancer tag.
Force a balancer in the running core to always pick one outbound (RoutingService.OverrideBalancerTarget). Applied live without a restart; cleared automatically when Xray restarts.

target.description: Outbound tag to force. Empty clears the override and returns control to the strategy.

post.summary: Ask the running core which outbound its router would pick for a synthetic connection (RoutingService.TestRoute). No traffic is sent.

domain.description: Target domain. Either domain or ip is required.

ip.description: Target IP. Either domain or ip is required.

protocol.description: Sniffed protocol such as http, tls, bittorrent (optional).

get.summary: List all outbound subscriptions (remote URLs that supply additional outbounds), newest first.

post.summary: Create an outbound subscription. The URL is fetched, parsed into outbounds with stable tags, and merged additively into the running Xray config.

url.description: Subscription URL (required). Must be a public http(s) address; private/internal targets are blocked unless allowPrivate is true.

tagPrefix.description: Prefix for generated outbound tags. Defaults to "sub<id>-".

enabled.description: Whether the subscription is active. Default true.

allowPrivate.description: Allow the URL to point at a private/internal/loopback address (localhost/LAN). Default false (SSRF guard blocks private targets).

prepend.description: Place this subscription's outbounds before the manual template outbounds (so one can become the default). Default false.

post.summary: Update an existing outbound subscription by id. Accepts the same form fields as create.

delete.summary: Delete an outbound subscription by id.

post.summary: Delete an outbound subscription by id (POST alias of DELETE for axios-friendly clients).
Force an immediate re-fetch of the subscription and return the parsed outbounds. Signals Xray to reload.
Reorder a subscription one step up or down in priority (controls its position in the merged outbounds).

dir.description: "up" to raise priority, anything else to lower it.

post.summary: Preview a subscription URL: fetch and parse it into outbounds without persisting anything.

get.summary: Return the current status of the Smart Outbound Auto-Failover Watchdog (active primary tag, candidates, failure counts, last failover).

post.summary: Immediately probe the active primary outbound and fail over to the fastest healthy candidate if unreachable.

get.summary: Return base64-encoded subscription links for all enabled clients matching the subscription ID. When the request has an Accept: text/html header or ?html=1, renders a styled info page instead. Default path: /sub/:subid.
Return subscription as a JSON array of proxy configs (one per enabled client). Only when JSON subscription is enabled in settings. Default path: /json/:subid.
Return subscription as a Clash/Mihomo-compatible YAML config, including configured global Clash routing rules. Only when Clash subscription is enabled in settings. Default path: /clash/:subid.
Every reseller with its live usage snapshot: inbound/client counts, allocated and consumed traffic and quota flags.
One reseller with the same usage snapshot as the list endpoint.

Ownership map for the admin UI: for every reseller, the inbound ids it owns and the client emails assigned to it directly. The display name and username are included so consumers (e.g. the clients page owner tags) can label the owner without a second request.
Full usage report of one reseller: usage snapshot and one row per client (quota, usage, attached inbounds).
Download one reseller client report as CSV (UTF-8 with BOM, CRLF rows, RFC 4180 quoting; traffic in binary GB).
Download the full resellers list with live usage numbers as CSV (UTF-8 with BOM; one row per reseller).

post.summary: Create a reseller. The password is hashed with bcrypt; a zero quota means "no limit". The username must differ from the panel admin and from every other reseller.

trafficLimit.description: Bytes. Cap on the sum of the reseller client quotas.

pricePerGb.description: GB-based billing price. Cost = used GB × pricePerGb; balance = deposit − cost. 0 (default) disables billing.

post.summary: Update a reseller. Send an empty (or omitted) password to keep the stored one.
Delete a reseller. Its inbounds and clients stay on the panel and fall back to the admin; ownership mappings and the ledger are removed.
Enable or disable a reseller. Disabling also turns off every inbound it owns and invalidates its active sessions.
Set a new password for a reseller and invalidate its sessions.
Hand an inbound (with all of its clients) to a reseller.
Return an inbound to the admin. Clients that only belonged to the reseller through this inbound go back with it; explicitly assigned clients stay.
Atomically add a batch of inbounds to a reseller; missing ids or an ownership conflict reject the whole batch.
Atomically remove a batch of inbound mappings for a reseller without changing inbound configuration.

Atomically replace the reseller inbound assignment set. Send the complete multi-select (an empty inboundIds array clears only this reseller); conflicts with another reseller or missing ids reject the whole transaction.
Atomically add explicit client visibility mappings for a reseller.
Atomically remove explicit client visibility mappings without deleting clients or inbound attachments.
Assign a single client (by email) to a reseller. Used for clients that live on a shared inbound owned by the admin.
Remove an explicit client assignment.
Top up (positive amount) or settle (negative amount) a reseller balance and append the movement to its ledger. A withdrawal cannot push the balance below zero.

get.summary: The signed-in reseller own profile and live usage snapshot.

post.summary: Update the signed-in reseller own brand name, logo, accent color, visual theme, and optional custom subscription domain. Branding is shown in the reseller workspace and public registration/deposit pages.

get.summary: Same payload as /panel/api/reseller/profile — alias used by the reseller dashboard.
The signed-in reseller own usage/billing report (clients + ledger).
Download the signed-in reseller own client report as CSV (UTF-8 with BOM, CRLF rows, RFC 4180 quoting; traffic in binary GB).

post.summary: Change the signed-in reseller own password. The old password is verified first; the session is cleared afterwards because the login epoch is bumped.

get.summary: Identity of the caller, so the SPA can render the right navigation: role is admin or reseller.

post.summary: Revoke and regenerate the subscription token (subId) for the client across all attached inbounds.

get.summary: List all reusable client plan templates.

post.summary: Create a reusable client plan template.
Update an existing client plan template.
Delete a client plan template.

get.summary: List all reseller support tickets (admin only).
Get a reseller support ticket and its message thread (admin only).

post.summary: Post an admin reply to a reseller support ticket.
Close a reseller support ticket (admin only).

get.summary: List processed payment webhook orders (admin only).

post.summary: Manually process an idempotent payment order (reseller deposit, quota top-up, or client renewal).

get.summary: List the signed-in reseller own support tickets.
Get a support ticket and its message thread owned by the signed-in reseller.

post.summary: Open a new support ticket as the signed-in reseller.
Post a reply to a support ticket owned by the signed-in reseller.
Close a support ticket owned by the signed-in reseller.

get.summary: List all reseller wallet gift/voucher codes.

post.summary: Create a new single-use or multi-use reseller wallet/traffic gift voucher code.
Delete a reseller gift voucher code by ID.
Redeem a gift/voucher code to credit the signed-in reseller wallet balance and/or traffic quota.

get.summary: The signed-in reseller's in-panel notification feed (newest first) with the unread count. Rows carry a kind (quota80, quota95, quota_out, climit80, climit_max, expiry_soon, expired) and a JSON params map for localized rendering.

post.summary: Flag one notification (body id > 0) or every unread notification (id omitted/0) of the signed-in reseller as read.

id.description: Notification id, or 0/omitted to mark all as read.

post.summary: Issue a fresh one-time Telegram link code for the signed-in reseller; sending "/start reseller_<code>" to the panel bot binds their Telegram chat.
Detach the signed-in reseller Telegram account from the panel bot.

get.summary: List plan templates whose inbound assignments are all owned by the signed-in reseller; only these templates can be offered through public registration links.

post.summary: Generate a signed registration link, valid for 30 days, for one eligible template. The link creates a client under the reseller and enforces client and traffic quotas.
Generate a signed public wallet top-up link for the signed-in reseller. The link expires after one year and is available while public checkout is enabled.
Run an Iran & international Check-Host TCP port or ICMP ping reachability test against a target host or host:port.

get.summary: List all panel admin accounts and their RBAC roles/permissions (owner only).

post.summary: Create a new panel admin account with an RBAC role and granular permissions (owner only).
Update a panel admin account RBAC role, permissions, or status (owner only).
Delete a secondary panel admin account (owner only).

get.summary: Fetch the reseller display name, configured payment currency, and optional white-label brand details for a signed top-up link.

post.summary: Create a pending wallet deposit order for an amount between 0.01 and 1,000,000. Up to 10 pending orders per reseller are allowed.

amount.description: Deposit amount in configured checkout currency.

get.summary: Poll the payment state of an order owned by the reseller referenced by the signed link.

parameters.name: orderId
parameters.description: Order ID returned by the order endpoint.

get.summary: Get the reseller display name, optional white-label brand details, and safe public plan details for a registration token.

post.summary: Register a new client using the invitation plan. Duplicate identifiers are rejected and reseller client/traffic limits are checked before client creation.

get.summary: Fetch the linked client status (enabled/expiry/quota/used) and the checkout pricing for the public page.

post.summary: Create a pending order for the linked client: extra traffic (gb) and/or renewal months (each = 30 days). Max 10 pending orders per client; amount must be > 0.

get.summary: Poll one order payment state for the linked client; orders that belong to another client report "unknown".

parameters.name: orderId
parameters.description: Order id from the order call.

get.summary: Upgrade an HTTP connection to a WebSocket. Requires an authenticated session cookie (Bearer token auth is not supported here). Returns 101 Switching Protocols on success. The server then pushes JSON messages described below.

ws.summary: Server health snapshot pushed every 2 seconds. Contains CPU, memory, swap, disk, network IO, load, and Xray state — same shape as GET /panel/api/server/status.
Xray process state change. Fired when Xray starts, stops, or encounters an error.
In-panel toast notification. Fired on Xray stop/restart, DB import, panel restart, etc.
Instructs the UI to re-fetch a resource. Fired when another admin session modifies data (e.g. toggling inbound enable).
